To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have designed a new attack algorithm for BNNs that is more effective than the state-of-the-art, that we have shown how to use this algorithm to design an attack on a real-world system (an autonomous car), that this attack can be thwarted using a simple defense technique, and that we have shown that the same defense technique also works against the state-of-the- art attack algorithm.
BNNs are vulnerable to adversarial attacks.

1) we present a new attack algorithm that exploits the structure of BNNs to generate adversarial examples that are effective in fooling BNNs, 2) we show that BNNs are significantly more sensitive to attacks than their floating point counterparts and 3) our attacks have a low computational cost and can be applied in real-time.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions:
    1. How can we design effective attacks against BNNs, and what are the limitations of such attacks?
    2. What is the relationship between adversarial robustness of BNNs and their computational efficiency?
    3. How can we use adversarial attacks to design robust BNNs?
two aspects of BNNs: (a) developing effective attacks that exploit the unique properties of these networks, and (b) designing new BNN architectures that are resilient to such attacks.
the following questions: (i) How to efficiently attack BNNs? (ii) How to defend against such attacks? and (iii) What is the impact of the binarization process on the robustness of BNNs?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Binarized Neural Network (BNNs), which is a special kind of neural network with binary weights, is vulnerable to adversarial attacks.

the proposed attack algorithm is a very effective attack method for binarized neural networks, and it can be used to generate adversarial examples that fool binarized neural network classifiers with very high success rates.
there is no single best way to train a BNN.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose two new attacks on binarized neural networks.
we have designed a novel class of attacks on BNNs, and have shown that these attacks are significantly more effective than existing attacks.
we show that the current binarization techniques are vulnerable to adversarial examples, and we present two new attacks, namely, the Bit-Flipping Attack (BFA) and the Bit-Weighting Attack (BWA).
The main takeaway from our work is that
BNNs are more vulnerable to adversarial attacks than fully connected neural networks (FNNs).
BNNs are particularly vulnerable to attacks that exploit the structure of the binarization process.
, despite being computationally efficient, BNNs are highly vulnerable to adversarial attacks.
